budget.note: 128 is the number of tools the Copilot agent-mode client can enable at once. Tool definitions are loaded into every request, so the token estimate below is a recurring cost, not a one-off cost. Counts marked estimated are vendor-documented figures, not measurements taken by this extension. Every shipped preset stays at or below 20 toolkit tools and leaves at least 20 tools of headroom. A third-party entry names the exact tools it selects and its count is the length of that list; a preset may not offer a surface whose tools the toolkit cannot name from a reviewed source.

presets.label: Read and cite a document
presets.goal: Open one workspace PDF, DOCX or Markdown file, read bounded text with page or paragraph locators, and write a cited Markdown or DOCX report.
tips: Smallest surface: four tools, so the assistant almost always picks the right one.
Use this when you are working on a single source, not searching a corpus.
requires: Managed worker installed in this workspace

presets.label: Search my own notes
presets.goal: Find passages across the Markdown and text files you select in this workspace, then reopen the matching passage with its paragraph provenance.
tips: Search results are local BM25 hits with file and line provenance; no index file is written.
read_text_source reopens a hit with adjacent paragraphs; read_document handles PDF and DOCX instead.
requires: Managed worker installed in this workspace

presets.label: Verify a citation
presets.goal: Check that a DOI resolves against Crossref and compare candidate references from the OpenAlex, Crossref and Semantic Scholar providers.
tips: An unresolved DOI is not proof that a citation is wrong; it means Crossref did not return it.
Network access to the public metadata APIs is required.
requires: Managed worker installed in this workspace
Network access to public metadata APIs

presets.label: Prepare a Zotero import
presets.goal: Collect references, read your Zotero collections and items, and create a new RIS file under research/imports/ for a manual import you review.
tips: Nothing is written to Zotero: the toolkit only creates a RIS file you import yourself.
Zotero must be running with its localhost API enabled for the collection and item tools.
requires: Managed worker installed in this workspace
Zotero localhost API for the Zotero tools

presets.label: Read, search, cite and write
presets.goal: The complete document and metadata surface in one preset: local document reading and search, scholarly metadata, Zotero reading, and cited report writing. No corpus index or record store.
tips: Recommended default: nine tools, well inside the range where tool selection stays reliable.
Choose corpus-lab or research-workflow when you need the stored index and claims.
requires: Managed worker installed in this workspace
Network access for the metadata tools
Zotero localhost API for the Zotero tools

presets.label: Full research workflow (index, evidence, claims)
presets.goal: The continuous Full journey in one preset: read a source, index the sources you select, retrieve a passage, resolve the evidence behind it, record a claim linked to that evidence, and write a cited report.
tips: Full default: fifteen toolkit tools, inside the 20-tool release budget and far below the 128-tool client ceiling.
The index, the retrieval vectors and the claims live in .research-toolkit/store/research.sqlite3 in this workspace; source files are never modified.

search_corpus takes mode lexical | vector | hybrid. hybrid fuses the stored BM25 ranking with the toolkit's own lexical-signature vectors; it is not an embedding model and installs no third-party database.
embed_corpus builds the stored vectors from the chunk text already in the store, on CPU, with no model download and no network call.
requires: Managed worker installed in this workspace
Corpus index and record store step completed

presets.label: Index, search and record claims
presets.goal: Index the Markdown, text, PDF or DOCX sources you select, search that stored corpus with page or paragraph provenance, resolve evidence, check that the indexed files are still the files on disk, and keep each claim linked to the exact chunks that support it.
tips: The index and claims live in .research-toolkit/store/research.sqlite3 in this workspace; source files are never modified.
A PDF chunk carries its original page number and offsets in that page's extracted text; a DOCX chunk carries its ordered paragraph or table-row item. A chunk never crosses a page or an item.

search_corpus takes mode lexical | vector | hybrid; embed_corpus builds or rebuilds the stored vectors. The vector ranker is a lexical signature over the stored text, not a semantic model, and every hit says which ranker contributed.
Lexical and vector retrieval are local. No embedding model is downloaded and no third-party database is installed by this preset.
requires: Managed worker installed in this workspace
Corpus index and record store step completed

presets.label: Maximum research: GitHub full plus the whole store
presets.goal: Work that lives in repositories — code, commits, issues, pull requests, releases, alerts — read and acted on through the full GitHub surface, while every finding is indexed, retrieved, cited and recorded in this workspace's research store.
tips: Widest shipped surface: 16 toolkit tools + 92 named GitHub tools = 108, exactly the 20 tools of headroom the budget keeps.

The five toolkit verbs this goal leaves out are named: search_local_text (the stored index is its search surface), zotero_write and prepare_zotero_import (a repository-centred goal does not write a reference library), unindex_corpus and store_maintenance (the destructive pair lives in corpus-lab and research-max-no-github).
The GitHub numbers are vendor catalog names, not measurements: no GitHub MCP server was started here. Confirm the real count with tools/list on your host.
Nothing is installed or configured by this preset. It is a plan; the Configure Preset Tools for Copilot command is what writes a selection, and it writes no credential.

presets.label: Maximum research: GitHub as read-only evidence
presets.goal: Read GitHub as a source you cite — a file, a commit, a release, an issue or a pull request, plus the read-only security and quality alerts around a repository — with no write, comment, push, merge or delete capability in the tool surface, and record what you found in the local store.
tips: 20 toolkit tools + 42 named GitHub tools = 62, leaving 66 tools of headroom.
Every GitHub name here is read-only, and the selection also sets the server's own read-only switch and lists every write tool as excluded.
The one toolkit verb this goal leaves out is store_maintenance: reading evidence does not need a vacuum or a restore.
Read-only in the tool surface is not a permission boundary: what your token may do is decided by GitHub, not by this preset.

thirdParty.label: GitHub MCP, read-only evidence selection
thirdParty.note: Every name here carries GitHub's own read-only hint; the server-side read-only switch and the explicit exclude list of all 35 write tools sit under it. Names are vendor-documented, not measured here, and a read-only switch is a filter, not a permission boundary. The 42 names are a chosen subset, not the whole published read-only set: the 35 published write tools are named as excluded, 14 further read-only names are not offered because their toolsets are not enabled in this preset, and `ui_get` is left out by choice rather than by the read-only rule.

presets.label: Maximum research: the whole local store, no GitHub
presets.goal: The complete local research surface in one preset: read sources, index them, build and search their retrieval vectors, resolve and re-verify evidence, record and export claims, read and write your local Zotero library, and maintain the store — with no third-party GitHub surface at all.
tips: 20 toolkit tools, no third-party surface: 108 tools of headroom under the 128-tool ceiling.
The one verb it leaves out is search_local_text: the goal is the stored corpus, and search_corpus is its search verb.

This preset configures nothing. To take Copilot's built-in GitHub server out of the surface, uncheck the GitHub group in Chat: Open Customizations -> Tools, and do not add a github entry to your MCP configuration.
store_maintenance and unindex_corpus are here: the preset that owns the store also owns its destructive verbs, each behind its own confirmation.
